Hi Clara — thanks for the heads up and context. We can support the 4/15 target; below are three pragmatic paths with tradeoffs. I've attached a short pricing matrix (lumina_pricing_options_v2.xlsx).

1) Temporary top-up (30–60 days) — fast to provision, billed as overage. No commit required. Typical lead time: 48–72 hrs.
   - Ideal when you want capacity immediately and minimal contract change
   - Unit cost: +35% over committed unit price

2) Staged-topup with conversion window — reserve capacity for the surge, with a 30-day conversion window to annualize a % of the top-up and co-term to Jan renewal. If converted, we credit back a portion of the overage and apply a discounted committed rate.
   - Lead time: 3–5 business days to provision reserve capacity
   - Conversion credit: up to 40% of top-up charges if converted within window

3) Annualize upfront (preferred for predictability) — convert X months of uplift into an annual add-on immediately and apply a promotional uplift discount tied to term and volume.
   - Lead time: depends on PO/signature cadence; we can provision earlier with an MOP (memorandum of performance)

Ben (cc'd) will pull exact numbers for Lumina's footprint and a proposed partial-annualization path. Karthik can run a quick performance check to confirm latency profile at the larger concurrency.

If you want, we can do a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to align on which path matches your risk tolerance.

—Naomi

Clara — following Naomi's note, I pulled three concrete proposals (estimates below are illustrative; final numbers in attached sheet).

Option A — Overage top-up (fastest)
- Capacity: +150k token-hours/month for 60 days
- Pricing: billed at 1.35x committed unit cost
- No long-term commitment

Option B — Staged-topup with 30d conversion
- Reserve: +150k token-hours for 60 days held as reserved capacity
- Conversion: if you annualize >=50% of the reserve within 30 days, we issue a credit equal to 35% of the reserve spend and apply committed pricing on converted volume for remaining term (co-term to Jan renewal).
- Benefit: avoids double-billing and gives time to validate production load

Option C — Partial annualize now
- Convert 6 months' expected uplift into an annual add-on (prorated to Jan renewal)
- Promotional uplift discount: 20% off committed unit price for the converted portion if signed by 4/10
- Includes one month of usage credit (trial) limited to 100k tokens

Recommended short path: start with Option B so we can provision quickly and preserve optionality. If Lumina signs partial annualization by 4/10 we can offer the Option C promo.

Executive summary for exception request:
- Customer: Lumina Health (Strategic mid-market account; currently on standard annual commit; renewal Jan 2028)
- Ask: Temporary staged-topup to start by 4/15 + higher conversion economics (50% credit) or 150k token pilot credit
- Rationale: Ability to validate at scale quickly will materially increase probability of converting uplift to annual commit and expanding committed footprint next year; procurement needs a clear amendment template to execute fast
- Risk: Short-term revenue take versus longer-term expansion; we mitigate via conversion window and co-term requirement

Proposal (recommended): Approve one-time exception — allow 50% conversion credit for staged-topup if Lumina signs partial annualization within 30 days AND commits to minimum 6-month converted volume (prorated to Jan co-term). If approved, I'll send an amendment template and Ben will coordinate PO cadence.

Requested by: EOD 4/05 to keep provision timeline for 4/15.
